def test_drain_alive_refusal_must_keep_owned_and_unrelated_processes(self):
        value = phases()
        value["drain-alive"]["processes"]["owned"]["alive"] = False
        value["drain-alive"]["processes"]["unrelated"]["after"]["alive"] = False
        checks, problems = harness.build_checks(value)
        self.assertFalse(checks["drain_alive_refused"])
        self.assertTrue(problems)
evidence.reason: The test mutates both independent process-preservation fields in a single fixture before calling `build_checks`. If either the owned-process check or the unrelated-process check were removed from the verifier, the remaining check would still make `drain_alive_refused` false, so this test would still pass and would not catch that regression. Splitting the two mutations into separate subtests with a fresh `phases()` fixture is the minimal routine test fix.
